answer: Because the pigment index resolves every citation against the whisper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the sonnet audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 251 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 251 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 4899 identities would post 1637 proofs and burn roughly 67 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
